summary: Enterprise request: Runtime LTS channel availability + support window and patch SLA (Dedicated/Private readiness)
description:
Customer (Northstar Bank) asked for formal confirmation of a Long Term Support (LTS) channel for the Redwood serving runtime as a blocker for their change-control and procurement process.

Request details (from customer):
- Need a stable runtime baseline supported for 12 months (minimum 6 months acceptable only with clear renewal/overlap). They explicitly do NOT want to be forced onto feature releases to receive security fixes.
- Patch cadence: monthly patch releases on the LTS line. They want to know if patches are optional vs mandatory, and how we communicate that.
- Security patch SLA: customer requested written commitment for critical vulnerabilities (customer phrasing: “high/critical CVEs”) with an out-of-band patch within 72 hours of confirmation, plus disclosure / comms process.
- Backport policy: eligibility criteria and approval process (who signs off, risk scoring, testing gates). They want assurances that backports are minimal diff, heavily tested, and do not introduce performance regressions.
- Artifact verification: Private deployment requires checksums/signatures and a way to map the runtime image to a commit/release note entry. SBOM request came up in their security questionnaire.
- Upgrade & rollback guidance: required for Private/VPC rollout, including validation checklist and what to collect for support.

Business context:
- Northstar is a regulated bank and indicated the LTS policy and patch SLA are a procurement gating item. Their platform team is preparing to move from Dedicated to a Private (VPC) deployment over the next two quarters.

Internal routing requested:
- Please confirm whether Redwood is planning an LTS channel and provide customer-facing language covering: support window, cadence, backport scope, security patch SLA, and artifact provenance.

Next steps proposed by Support:
- Route to Release Engineering + Runtime leadership for authoritative commitments.
- Provide customer with (1) draft LTS policy summary, (2) timeline for first LTS branch availability, and (3) a short FAQ for procurement/security review.

Attachments/links:
- Notes captured from customer call were shared in #support and forwarded to #eng-releases for confirmation.
- Related customer pain: they cited an earlier latency regression after a runtime upgrade as motivation for pinning (see SUP-18477).

Support intake checklist completed:
- Customer asked for written commitments; no runtime logs requested at this time (policy/process request).
comments: 2025-01-29 (Jasmine Liu, Reporter): Created per Northstar platform team request. They want an LTS commitment in writing for change-control. Adding Dev Patel to drive the support response and coordinate internally.

2025-01-29 (Dev Patel, Assignee): Acknowledged. Routing to Release Eng / Runtime for authoritative answer. Looping in Connor O’Brien (Release Eng), Mateo Alvarez (VP Eng Runtime), and Dr. Aisha Rahman (security policy sponsor). Will propose customer-facing language we can stand behind.

2025-01-30 (Connor O’Brien): We’re actively standing up Runtime LTS. Not ready to promise dates publicly until ADR is approved, but direction is: runtime-1.18-lts branch with monthly patch cadence + out-of-band security fixes. Support window target is 12 months with 3-month overlap between LTS lines. Backport policy: security + Sev1 + select Sev2 only; minimal diffs; perf gates required. I’ll provide draft language for customer.

2025-01-30 (Mateo Alvarez): Confirmed directionally yes. For commitments: we can state intent + process now; specific SLA numbers need Security sign-off. For backports/perf: LTS will have stricter gating than mainline (scheduler smoke + perf canary).

2025-01-31 (Dr. Aisha Rahman): For security SLAs: we can offer tiered response language (e.g., critical remote code execution or credential exposure gets expedited out-of-band). Exact timelines should be aligned with Hanae Suzuki (vuln response coordination) and existing enterprise security commitments. Suggest wording: “as soon as practicable, target within X business days” unless contractually committed. If Northstar needs 72 hours, that likely needs to be a contracted term for Private/Dedicated.

2025-02-03 (Dev Patel): Drafted response for customer (internal review) covering: (1) LTS support window target 12 months, (2) monthly patch cadence + out-of-band security, (3) backport eligibility and approvals, (4) reproducible artifacts w/ checksums (SBOM in progress). Sending to Connor + Rachel Kim for CS alignment and Avery Johnson for sales/procurement language.

2025-02-05 (Rachel Kim): From CS perspective: Northstar will likely accept “12 months support” + clear comms, but will press on security patch SLA. Recommend we position 72-hour as a contractual SLA option for Private/Dedicated with premium support. Also highlight rollback guidance and “mandatory patch” criteria to reduce operational surprises.

2025-02-07 (Avery Johnson): Northstar procurement wants a one-pager. Please keep language crisp and avoid “best effort” wording if possible. If we can’t commit to 72h universally, we should offer a clear escalation path and an option to contract the timeline.

2025-02-10 (Connor O’Brien): Updated: ADR for branching/versioning is in approval. We can state branch naming convention and support window, and that release artifacts will include checksums/provenance. Artifact signing/SBOM is planned (phased). Provided customer-facing draft language and pointed to docs PR in progress.

2025-02-12 (Dev Patel): Sent customer response (via CSM/AEs) with:
- Runtime LTS channel planned with a stable branch (runtime-1.18-lts) and monthly patch releases.
- Backport scope: security + critical correctness fixes only; features generally not backported.
- Testing: CI + targeted scheduler regression suite + perf canary gates; releases include known issues and rollback guidance.
- Artifact verification: checksums/provenance metadata; SBOM support is planned.
- Security patch handling: out-of-band security patches; exact SLA to be addressed in contract language for enterprise tier.
Awaiting confirmation from Northstar that this meets procurement needs; they may come back with a specific SLA ask.

2025-02-18 (Dev Patel): Customer confirmed this is sufficient to proceed to the next procurement step, with an open item for contractual security patch SLA. Marking ticket Resolved; follow-up tracked with Sales/CS. If they request an explicit 72-hour SLA, route through Security + Legal for contract addendum.
resolution: Provided Northstar with Redwood’s LTS channel plan and customer-facing policy summary (support window target, monthly patch cadence, backport scope/approvals, testing/perf gates, and artifact verification direction). Security patch SLA details flagged as a contractual term for enterprise. Customer indicated the response unblocked procurement to proceed pending contract language.
customer_next_steps: Northstar to review procurement docs and return with any required security patch SLA language for contract negotiation; schedule a follow-up technical session on Private upgrade/rollback and artifact verification requirements.
internal_follow_ups: Align standardized customer-facing LTS commitment language with Security/Legal (include optional contracted security patch SLA). Owner: Avery Johnson + Dr. Aisha Rahman.
Publish Runtime LTS docs (branching/backport policy + release notes format + Private pinning/rollback guidance). Owner: Elliot Price / Kira Thompson.
Ensure LTS artifacts include checksums/provenance and document verification steps; track SBOM rollout. Owner: Sahana Iyer.
